text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: prod-kv-paged pool memory pressure spike detected. avg free memory per pod < 600MB, latency 95p > 2s, error_rate 4.8%. Triggering incident channel.

Alex (oncall): Seeing the same in grafana. Heap/kv block growth looks correlated with continuous-batching rollout from last night. I can reproduce allocation spikes when batches > 16.

Priya (sre): Confirmed. Heap growth graph: `block_metadata_map` cardinality rising steadily — looks like something isn't being freed during evictions. Suspect metadata leak tied to new batch coalescing path.

Jae (eng-runtime): On it. Hypothesis: when batch coalescer merges overlapping prefixes, it writes a temporary index into block metadata and failing to clear on eviction path. I'll instrument but need immediate mitigation.

Marta (customer-success): FYI one customer (AcmeRetail) reported 503s and slow responses affecting checkout meta calls. They're on a dedicated pool but traffic hit prod-kv-paged for fallback. Customer is notified and we offered to throttle.

Alex (oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) lower continuous batch size 2) tighten eviction policy 3) recycle the problematic pool to reclaim memory. I'm going to apply 1 and 2 as a hotfix.

Priya (sre): Agree. Patch plan: update runtime config on prod-kv-paged selector `pool=kv-paged` with `batch_size: 8 -> 4`, `kv.block_manager.eviction_policy: balanced -> aggressive`, `kv.block_manager.block_size: 4MB -> 2MB` for this rollout. This should reduce per-pod memory pressure and accelerate eviction.

Jae (eng-runtime): Quick patch ready. Command I'm going to run:
```
# dry-run
rctl patch runtime --selector pool=kv-paged --set batch.coalesce.max_items=4 --set block_manager.eviction=aggressive --set block_manager.block_size=2m --env prod --dry-run
# apply
rctl patch runtime --selector pool=kv-paged --set batch.coalesce.max_items=4 --set block_manager.eviction=aggressive --set block_manager.block_size=2m --env prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-serving -l pool=kv-paged -n redwood-prod
```

InfraBot: NOTE: k8s rolling restart will restart 20 pods with maxUnavailable=2. Expect transient latency increase ~30s per pod.

Alex (oncall): Proceed with patch and monitor. I'll keep on-call window and watch error_rate/latency dashboards. Priya, set alert if error_rate > 5% for 10m.

Priya (sre): Patch applied at 1959876590. Observability: within 90s mem per pod started dropping, eviction counts increased. 95p latency trending down from 2.1s -> 1.05s. Error rate dropped to 1.2% in the first 5m.

Jae (eng-runtime): Added temporary guard in runtime to aggressively clear `block_metadata_map` on eviction as a belt-and-suspenders measure. This is a config toggle `block_manager.force_metadata_trim=true`. I applied it to the selector as well.

Sam (eng-runtime-lead): Good quick mitigation, but we need a proper patch. Do a postmortem with surface area: coalescer path, eviction correctness, and run a fuzzer for batch coalescing. Also capture heap profiles from the affected pods for the last 48h.

Marta (customer-success): Update for AcmeRetail: latency back within SLOs and they accepted the mitigation. They've requested a short postmortem and confirmation this won't recur. I'll coordinate follow-up.

Alex (oncall): Noted. Current status: customer impact reduced to minimal, pool stable. However, memory hasn't fully reclaimed on two older pods — I'm doing a manual drain+delete on those nodes to force fresh pods.

Priya (sre): Ran heapdump collection from the restarted pods and uploaded to S3: `s3://redwood-dumps/1959876543/`. Captured `pprof` and `jeprof` snapshots.

Jae (eng-runtime): Found root cause in internal diff: coalescer introduced `MetaRef` objects that were appended to `block_metadata_map` but only removed on full-evict; under aggressive steady traffic they never hit full-evict. Patch in review to call `MetaRef.release()` during partial evict + unit tests added.

Alex (oncall): Please push the code hotfix to canary once tests pass, then schedule a controlled rollout. For now keep `force_metadata_trim=true` as a 6-12 hour guard.

Priya (sre): Agreed. I'm removing the emergency aggressive eviction after mem stabilizes. For now the cluster is at: avg free mem 1.8GB, 95p latency 950ms, error rate 0.9%.

Sam (eng-runtime-lead): After hotfix lands: 1) revert temporary `block_size` shrink if perf regression shows throughput loss 2) instrument a gauge for `block_metadata_map.size` and alert at 1k entries per pod 3) add regression test in CI that simulates steady partial evictions during coalescing.

Marta (customer-success): I've scheduled a short sync with AcmeRetail for 1500 UTC to go over mitigations and follow-ups.

Alex (oncall): Handoff notes for next oncall (Jae covering until 03:00Z): monitor `prod-kv-paged` memory, `block_metadata_map` gauge, and error_rate. Escalate to Sam if error_rate > 3% for 15m or memory per pod < 800MB for 10m.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 1959876800. Postmortem requested within 48h.

Jae (eng-runtime): I'll take postmortem lead. Preliminary action items: code patch to MetaRef lifecycle (PR #3721), add e2e with partial-evict workload, add alert + dashboard, verify block_size defaults across pools, and schedule a follow-up deployment window.

Priya (sre): I'll attach heap profiles and the hotfix rollout timestamps to the incident doc. Link: https://redwood-internal/incident/1959876543

Sam (eng-runtime-lead): Thanks team. Nice work on quick mitigation and customer comms. We'll aim to close after root cause patch lands and a successful canary.

Alex (oncall): Closing thread for immediate mitigation. Handoff note repeated: Jae owns monitoring until 03:00Z. Please ping oncall if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
